atencao-esparsa.d: Attention in which each query computes scores for only a subset of the keys (a window, a top-k picked by an indexer, or compressed entries) instead of all of them. It reduces what is read and computed; it only reduces what is stored if the KV is compressed as well.

swa.d: Attention that only sees the last \(W\) tokens (sliding_window). Cost \(O(W)\) per token and constant KV per sequence, stored in a ring; it forgets on purpose, which complicates prefix caching (the old blocks are freed).

campo-receptivo.d: How many past positions can influence a token. With windows of \(W\) across \(L\) layers, the theoretical reach is \(L(W-1)+1\), but distant information arrives diluted, after passing through several weighted sums.

ring-buffer.d: A fixed-size circular buffer of \(W\) slots, addressed by slot = position mod \(W\): new data overwrites the oldest. It's how sliding windows are stored (DeepSeek: 128 per layer), as well as the tail of GLM's kpool indexer (4 positions).

lightning-indexer.d: The cheap scorer of DSA-style sparse attention: a few 128-dimensional heads, one shared key per token, low precision (FP8/FP4) and ReLU instead of softmax. It computes \(I_{t,s}=\sum_h w_{t,h}\,\mathrm{ReLU}(q^I_{t,h}\cdot k^I_s)\) and picks the top-k keys for the main attention.

dsa.d: The sparse attention that debuted in DeepSeek-V3.2: a lightning indexer (64 heads × 128) picks 2,048 tokens per query and MLA attends only to those. GLM-5.3-Flash uses the same idea over pools of 4 keys.

nsa.d: DeepSeek's trainable sparse attention proposal, with three branches summed by learned gates: attention over block summaries, fine attention over the selected blocks and a sliding window, at block granularity. GLM's kernel in FlashInfer inherited the name (GLM_NSA).

selecao-top-k.d: Keeping the \(k\) largest values of a score vector (and their indices). It isn't differentiable and depends on ties and rounding; on the GPU it is a kernel of its own (persistent_topk, top_k_per_row_decode) with shared memory limits.

qsa.d: Qwen3.8's sparse attention, in 12 of its 48 layers: an indexer with 4 heads × 128 and 1 shared key scores micro-blocks of 4 tokens (mean + RMSNorm + RoPE), picks 512 blocks (2,048 positions) plus the tail of up to 3 tokens, and runs a GQA over the original K/V of those positions.

kpool.d: GLM-5.3-Flash's DSA indexer, which groups the keys into pools of index_kpool = 4 tokens through a learned pooling (gate softmax + per-slot positional bias), followed by Hadamard-128 and FP8: 132 B per pool. It picks select_k = 512 pools (≈ 2,048 tokens) plus the tail.

kpool-tail.d: GLM's KV group that stores, per request, a single circular block of 4 positions with the keys and gates of the up to 3 tokens that haven't closed a pool yet. It doesn't take part in prefix caching and needs special slot mapping and strides.

compressor-kv.d: The DeepSeek-V4 module that summarizes blocks of 4 or 128 tokens into one KV entry through a learned, gated pooling: a per-channel softmax over the block's positions (8 positions with overlap in C4), followed by RMSNorm, RoPE at the first token's position and FP8. In decode it accumulates partial state and only emits when the block closes.

csa-hca.d: DeepSeek-V4's two compressed attentions. CSA/C4A compresses the KV 4:1 and a lightning indexer picks 512 entries; HCA/C128A compresses 128:1 and reads every entry. Both add a sliding window of 128 raw tokens, in a single softmax.

destilacao-indexador.d: Training the indexer as a student of the model's own dense attention, minimizing \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\,\|\,\mathrm{softmax}(I))\). It happens in two phases: a dense warmup (model frozen) and joint sparse training (top-k switched on). It works around the fact that top-k isn't differentiable.

massa-de-atencao.d: The fraction \(\sum_{s\in S} a_s\) of a head's dense attention distribution that falls on the chosen keys \(S\). If it is \(1-\varepsilon_h\), that head's sparse output differs from the dense one by at most \(2\varepsilon_h\max\|v\|\); with the average over heads, the bound holds on average.

sequence-parallel.d: Splitting the sequence axis (tokens or keys) across GPUs instead of replicating the work. In DeepSeek's indexer, each rank scores a slice of the compressed keys, runs a local top-k, and an all-gather of (score, id) enables the exact merge.

workspace-pre-alocado.d: Scratch memory a kernel or backend reserves up front (indexer logits, key gather, index buffers). vLLM measures it during the profile run and deducts it from the KV budget, so oversizing it costs context.

slot-mapping.d: The per-step conversion of a token's position into its physical slot in the KV cache: block_table[req, pos // block_size] · block_size + pos % block_size. An unbounded block index reads or writes another request's memory.

radix-select.d: Algorithm that finds the k-th largest value without sorting: it turns each FP32 score into an order-preserving integer key and fixes the threshold one byte at a time, with a 256-bin histogram per pass (4 passes for 32 bits). It uses only integer counts, so it is exact and deterministic. TensorFold uses it to pick the 512 pools of GLM's indexer.

indexador-em-pedacos.d: A variant of the prefill indexer that scores each request's rows in blocks bounded by a fixed logits budget (2 GiB of FP32 in the sglang#39187 backport), instead of a whole [rows × prefix] tensor. It trades a peak of ~14 B × chunk × prefix for a constant ceiling.
